Diff arithmetic

Ordered patches compose transitions with preconditions. Signed deltas add and subtract weighted graph facts. Separate C# types require an explicit conversion between them.

Contract illustration
Diff
◉ Active+ Added− RemovedΔ Changed× Rejected
The rule
What the contract requires
Patch composition requires adjacent compatible versions. Delta-to-patch conversion needs a base graph and validity checks.
The boundary
Scope and constraints
Signed-delta arithmetic permits negative weights. Materialization validates the resulting graph. Conversion reports any loss of chronology.
Example · C#
Subtract deltas, then choose a base
Full source ↗
Signed arithmetic and patch conversion are separate typed requests.
UsageExamples.cs
public static EvaluateDelta Subtract(SignedDelta left, SignedDelta right) =>
    new(new RequestId("subtract"),
        new DeltaSubtract(new DeltaLiteral(left), new DeltaLiteral(right)));

public static ConvertDeltaToPatch AtBase(
    SignedDelta delta, GraphVersion basis, GraphVersion target, ChangeCause cause) =>
    new(new RequestId("materialize"), new DeltaAtBase(delta, basis, cause), target);
// Matching tenant, projection and ontology are required. Applying a signed
// result also needs a base graph: negative fact counts can be rejected.
Compile-checked caller example. Execution requires implementations of the injected interfaces.
